name: ICAL (In-Context Abstraction Learning) — "VLM Agents Generate Their Own Memories: Distilling Experience into Embodied Programs of Thought"
authors_affiliation: Gabriel Sarch, Lawrence Jang, Michael J. Tarr, William W. Cohen, Kenneth Marino, Katerina Fragkiadaki. Carnegie Mellon University; Google DeepMind (Cohen and Marino).
maintained_repo_url: N/A (project website https://ical-learning.github.io/; no maintained leaderboard/paper-list)
task_domain: Multimodal/embodied agents and decision-making: dialogue-based household instruction following (embodied), multimodal autonomous web navigation, and egocentric video action forecasting.
problem_setting: Interactive, continual learning of a single VLM agent that transforms noisy/suboptimal demonstrations (from humans or its own policy) into high-quality, generalizable examples. Two phases: (1) an offline-style abstraction phase where a VLM corrects action errors and writes language+visual 'programs of thought'; (2) a human-in-the-loop phase where annotations are refined via natural-language feedback during execution in similar environments. Supervision is available as suboptimal demos plus non-expert human feedback. The learned example library is then used either for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) at test time or for supervised fine-tuning (SFT). Single-agent, private growing memory. (Ego4D is a passive setting using the abstraction phase only, no human-in-the-loop.)
what_is_retrieved: Abstracted experiences / cases: optimized trajectories paired with multimodal 'programs of thought' (generalized strategies, causal/task abstractions, object state changes, temporal subgoals, task-relevant visual elements / construals) plus the corresponding action sequence — stored as in-context demonstrations.
retrieval_grounding: GROWING/episodic memory the agent writes to itself (memory set M of self-distilled abstracted examples that grows during continual learning), rather than a static external corpus.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking objective: retrieve the top-K (K=5) most similar abstracted examples by aggregated similarity to inject into the prompt; no notion of recovering a complete minimal set or variable-size precision-driven recommendation.
cbr_cycle_coverage: Retrieve, Reuse, Revise, Retain (all four). Retrieve = top-K similar abstracted examples; Reuse = inject as in-context exemplars / SFT data; Revise = VLM self-refinement + human-in-the-loop correction of trajectory and thoughts; Retain = store successful refined example into M.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False — the work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner; it frames the mechanism as 'in-context abstraction learning', self-generated memories, and programs of thought, while in practice realizing CBR-like Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain dynamics. [uncertain] on absolute absence of any CBR citation.
retrieval_unit: A full abstracted example (case = problem-solution): an optimized trajectory plus its language/visual programs of thought. At deployment in VisualWebArena/Ego4D the in-context example is built around a single time step (image input + abstracted textual state + summary + step-by-step reasoning + predicted next state + abstraction comments + predicted action); an appendix variant uses the full trajectory.
index_source: Growing memory built online/at learning-time: examples are induced by abstracting noisy human or agent demonstrations and stored into memory set M, which grows continually as more demonstrations are processed; frozen at deployment when used purely for RAG/SFT (but grows during the learning loop).
index_structure_topology: Flat similarity index over example embeddings; retrieval by aggregated cosine similarity over three components (input instruction text, textual state, visual state). No graph/hierarchical/cluster topology.
retriever_type: Dense embedding retriever (off-the-shelf): OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002 for text and CLIP ViT-B/32 for images, combined via a weighted multi-modal cosine-similarity score. A reranking variant is also explored.
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf frozen embedders); the only tuned parameters are the per-domain similarity-weighting coefficients (lambda_I, lambda_textual, lambda_visual) chosen on a held-out validation set. The retriever itself is not contrastively trained or RL-optimized.
query_construction: Query is formed from the current context: the new task instruction I, the current textual state description (objects/attributes for embodied, HTML elements for web), and the current visual state (webpage image / video frames, Set-of-Marks annotated). Matched against stored example embeddings.
query_granularity: Both task-level and step/state-level: retrieval is conditioned on the instruction (task-level) and the current scene/state. In VisualWebArena/Ego4D deployment, top-5 examples are retrieved at each time step (step/state-level).
when_to_retrieve: Iterative / per-step at deployment (retrieve top-5 at each time step for web/embodied execution); also retrieves during the learning loop (abstraction and human-in-the-loop phases) to condition new abstractions on prior examples. Fixed schedule, not uncertainty-triggered.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule: retrieval happens deterministically at every decision step (and at each abstraction-generation step during learning); there is no learned router, confidence threshold, reflection token, or agent-initiated retrieval request.
reranking: Optional reranking stage explored as an ablation ('w/ retrieval re-ranking' on TEACh gave 35.3 SR / 51.7 GC vs 35.1 / 49.3 without); the main pipeline uses weighted multi-modal cosine similarity top-K without a dedicated cross-encoder reranker.
retrieved_context_refinement: None at retrieval time beyond the optional reranking; the retrieved items are themselves already-distilled/refined abstractions (refinement happens at write-time via self-refinement + human feedback, not as a post-retrieval step).
tool_document_engineering: N/A — ICAL retrieves experience examples, not tool/API documents.
index_content_separation: N/A — no lightweight-index-then-load-content / progressive-disclosure separation; embeddings index full abstracted examples directly.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A — not a tool-retrieval system; agent acts via a fixed action API (e.g., go_to(X), pickup(X)) / Python code, no RapidAPI/RESTful/MCP tool index.
how_retrieved_used: Two utilization modes: (1) prompt augmentation — the top-K retrieved abstracted examples are injected as in-context demonstrations for retrieval-augmented generation with a VLM (GPT-4V/GPT-4o/GPT-3.5); (2) training signal — the abstracted examples form a dataset for supervised fine-tuning (LoRA on GPT-3.5; full SFT of Qwen2-VL). The two can be combined (SFT + retrieval).
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-act with per-step interleaving: at each step the agent retrieves the top-5 abstracted examples and prompts the VLM to emit the next action (or a Python program over the action API) for embodied/web tasks; one-shot conditioning for the passive Ego4D forecasting. No MCTS/tree-search integration.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-tool-call / per-action-step within a rollout for interactive tasks (retrieve and re-prompt each step); per-answer for the passive Ego4D action-forecasting setting.
adaptation_mechanism: Execution-feedback-driven and human-in-the-loop revision at write-time, then mostly verbatim ICL reuse at deployment: a retrieved example is used as an in-context exemplar; the agent does not run an explicit per-query case-adaptation step at test time (adaptation/revision is what produced the stored example).
retrieved_item_representation: Distilled multimodal 'programs of thought': free-text strategy/causal abstractions, subgoal decomposition, predicted state changes and abstraction comments, task-relevant visual elements, plus the optimized action sequence (which can be executable code over the action API). Structured-note + executable-action hybrid.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Distilled strategy/insight and state-aware guideline level (causal abstractions, object state changes, temporal subgoals/decomposition, visual construals) layered on an optimized trajectory — explicitly contrasted against raw, unabstracted demonstrations.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Robustness comes from the abstraction/refinement pipeline rather than retrieval-time filtering: a VLM self-corrects action inefficiencies/errors in noisy trajectories, and human-in-the-loop natural-language feedback iteratively refines abstractions; only successful refined examples are retained, filtering bad experiences out of memory. Paper notes it can handle noisy demos but not extremely misleading ones.
memory_type: Episodic example library / skill-and-experience memory (memory set M of abstracted trajectory examples). Episodic-with-procedural-content.
write_back: True — successful refined trajectories and their thoughts are stored into the memory set M (M <- M ∪ {(xi_optimized, L)}); this self-generated memory is the core contribution ('VLM agents generate their own memories').
online_growth: True — the example library grows continually as new demonstrations are processed; the paper shows continual-learning/meta-learning effects (later examples require fewer environment steps and less human feedback). At pure test-time deployment the store is used as-is, but during the learning loop it grows online.
write_back_trigger: On-success only: after the human-in-the-loop phase, if the trajectory succeeds it is stored; if still unsuccessful after N_feedbacks iterations it is discarded and the agent moves on. (Appendix S4.5 explores relabeling partially-successful demos, which helps weaker models.)
failure_experience_usage: Success-only storage in the main method: failed/unsuccessful trajectories (after exhausting feedback iterations) are NOT stored or retrieved. Failures are used transiently as feedback signal to drive revision, not retained as negative cases. (An appendix variant relabels partially-successful demonstrations.)
memory_evolution_update: Append-only: successful abstracted examples are added to M (M <- M ∪ {...}); stored entries are not subsequently mutated, merged, pruned, or overwritten. (Earlier examples are retrieved to help abstract later ones, improving future abstractions, but already-stored entries themselves are not edited.)
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No — case selection is a fixed weighted-cosine-similarity top-K, not a learned/RL-optimized retrieval policy (only the per-domain similarity weights are tuned on validation).
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Single-agent private memory — the agent builds and uses its own example library; no cross-agent or cross-framework memory sharing.
benchmarks: TEACh (dialogue-based household instruction following, validation unseen/seen); VisualWebArena (multimodal autonomous web navigation; classifieds/Reddit/shopping); Ego4D v2 (egocentric long-term video action anticipation/forecasting).
baselines: HELPER (hand-written domain-expert examples; prior TEACh SOTA); Zero-Shot CoT; Raw Visual Demos (inverse-dynamics-labeled) and Raw Kinesthetic Demos (GT-action labeled); GPT-4V + Set-of-Marks (Koh et al., prior VisualWebArena SOTA), GPT-4o + SoM, Gemini-Pro-1.5, CogVLM, IDEFICS-80B-Instruct, base Qwen2-VL-7B; for Ego4D: few-shot GPT-4V with CoT and the fully-supervised SlowFast+Transformer baseline (Grauman et al. 2022).
key_metrics: TEACh: Success Rate (SR) and Goal-Condition success (GC). VisualWebArena: task success rate (seen/unseen/average). Ego4D: edit distance (Damerau-Levenshtein) over predicted verbs/nouns/actions. Plus efficiency metrics: environment steps and human feedbacks per example; scaling vs #examples.
headline_result: Across benchmarks ICAL sets SOTA: TEACh +12.6% goal-condition success over HELPER (and combined SFT+retrieval on ICAL examples beats raw human/expert demos by 17.5% GC); VisualWebArena task success improved 1.6x with retrieval-augmented GPT-4V (14.3% -> 22.7% avg) and fine-tuned Qwen2-VL 2.8x over base (2.9% -> 8.2%); Ego4D surpasses few-shot GPT-4V and is competitive with supervised models using 639x less in-domain training data; scales 2x better than raw demonstrations.
ablations: TEACh ablations (GPT-3.5): full ICAL retrieval 35.1 SR / 49.3 GC; w/o programs-of-thought (abstraction) phase 29.4 / 44.9; w/o human-in-the-loop 29.9 / 41.0; w/ retrieval re-ranking 35.3 / 51.7; w/ GPT-4 41.7 / 63.6; ICAL SFT 23.2 / 40.3; ICAL SFT + retrieval 35.8 / 54.2. VisualWebArena ablations (GPT-4V, 257-episode subset): ICAL 28.0/21.6/22.2 (seen/unseen/avg) vs GPT-4V 11.5/12.9/12.7; w/o image 28.0/17.3/19.0; w/ full text trajectory 57.7/21.6/25.5 (helps seen but not unseen, and costs more, so single-step+image used for final). Ablations show both the offline abstraction (programs-of-thought) phase and the human-in-the-loop phase are important.
evaluation_decoupling: No — only end-to-end task metrics (SR/GC, web success, edit distance) are reported; intrinsic retrieval metrics like Recall@k/nDCG are not reported separately (retrieval quality is assessed only via downstream task performance and a reranking ablation).
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome metrics (final task success / goal-condition success / action-forecasting edit distance), plus learning-process/efficiency metrics (environment steps per example, human feedbacks per example, scaling vs number of learned examples) that characterize the continual-learning dynamics rather than per-step reasoning faithfulness.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Continual-learning efficiency: in TEACh, the second half of examples required 38.8% fewer environment steps (436±88 -> 267±43, p=0.0143) and 71.6% less human feedback (0.74±0.17 -> 0.21±0.08, p=0.0089) per example; scales 2x better than raw demonstrations; only ~10 learned examples give +14.7% SR over zero-shot CoT; Ego4D competitive with supervised models using 639x less in-domain data. Appendix shows full-trajectory in-context examples raise cost (context length) without improving unseen success, so single-step+image retrieval is used. Uses K=5 retrieval.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k: top-K = 5 abstracted examples injected at each step (k=5 for example retrieval). Single time-step representation (image + abstracted state + reasoning + action) chosen over full-trajectory to bound context length / cost; not adaptive or budget-capped beyond the fixed k.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A — primary research paper, not a survey.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A — uses existing benchmarks (TEACh, VisualWebArena, Ego4D v2) rather than introducing one. (Data-efficiency note: ICAL learns from ~30 non-expert human demos in VisualWebArena and uses 639x less in-domain training data than the supervised Ego4D baseline.)
builds_on: HELPER (Sarch et al., embodied LLM agent with memory-augmented prompting / retrieval — extended as the TEACh execution backbone and baseline); VisualWebArena + GPT-4V + Set-of-Marks prompting (Koh et al.); set-of-marks visual prompting; in-context learning / chain-of-thought and self-reflection lines (e.g., Reflexion-style introspection); CLIP and OpenAI text embeddings for retrieval; LoRA fine-tuning; Qwen2-VL.
contrasts_with: Methods that only store/retrieve successful raw action plans or trajectories without distilled abstractions (HELPER, AdaPlanner-style, Synapse/trajectory-as-exemplar); text-only experience/insight methods that focus on reward signals or store human corrections only after failures; expert-hand-written example pipelines (HELPER requires 48-107 lines of expert text per example) and pure prompt-engineering approaches.
lineage: Group D (case-based / experience planning): a multimodal experience-distillation / self-generated-memory line that converts raw suboptimal trajectories into abstracted, retrievable insights stored in a growing example library for RAG or fine-tuning — sits between trajectory-memory agents (HELPER, Synapse, ExpeL) and procedural skill-library agents (Voyager), distinguished by cognitive abstractions (causal, state-change, subgoal, visual construal) and human-in-the-loop refinement.
